compiled_state.author: RebarBotNava
compiled_state.description:
Reduce rebar tickets-store growth and reclaim the ~1 GiB already spent, by making the
reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache cheap instead of re-homing it.

Measured facts, full research trail and the three corrected false premises: session_log
**1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Supersedes the tabled plan in
**bronze-used-foxhound** (e594-e1d0). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

The `tickets` branch is **1.04 GiB**; **92%** is the reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache, not
ticket data (events are 55 MB). Diffing consecutive committed revisions of `bindings.json`
(1509 bindings) shows the growth is bookkeeping nothing reads:

| field | entries changed per pass |
|---|---|
| `baseline` (the value) | **0** |
| `baseline_advanced_at` (written at `binding_store.py:375`, read nowhere in `src/`) | **1144** |
| `last_get_pass` (rotation bookkeeping) | **20** |

A scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file defeats git delta compression. Measured on 40
consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo and repacked `--window=250 --depth=50`, true
marginal cost per version is **12.79 KB** today, **1.74 KB** after deleting the timestamp (7.4x),
and the version count halves once rotation bookkeeping moves out (12.8x total).

## Approach and why this one

Keep the cache committed and make it cheap. `.bridge_state` must stay on-branch because the
reconciler runs on **ephemeral** GitHub-hosted runners, so durable state has to live in git — an
earlier design wrote prev to the main-branch worktree, so prev was always `{}` and the differ
re-derived 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`). Epic `6c9c` evaluated and
dropped re-homing it off-branch (WS-1) because the convergence loop already self-heals binding
drift. So the levers are content and churn, not location.

The one-time reclaim of existing history is included (child A6) under an operator-approved
quiescence protocol. Its mechanics are **proven, not theoretical**: `git fast-export --no-data |
filter | git fast-import` on the real branch produced 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%)
with all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges preserved and the HEAD tree byte-identical except the
intended paths. Stock git plumbing only — `git-filter-repo` is deliberately **not** used: it is an
unwanted core dependency and it prunes empty commits, which would reshape the DAG that
ancestry-based authorship verification walks.

## Scope (children, in dependency order)

1. **A1** delete `baseline_advanced_at` + write-when-changed guard in `set_baseline`
2. **A2-1** move `last_get_pass` to `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`; read `max(new, legacy)`
3. **A3** text-normalize baseline description/status/priority (exclude `assignee`)
4. **A2-2** delete the legacy in-line `last_get_pass` field (gated on writer rollout)
5. **A4-1/2/3** `bridge_fsck` fence, then `prev_snapshot` -> key-set, then branch-3 empty-payload skip
6. **A5** ADR covering all three committed-format changes
7. **A6** one-time reclaim under the quiescence protocol (LAST; requires A1-A5 and Epic B's B6)

## Compatibility and rollback

Three committed-format changes to a shared store file, each with a stated boundary. A2-1 is
reversible (it never stops writing the legacy field). A3 is reversible because the read path
canonicalizes both shapes idempotently. A2-2 and A4-2 are the irreversible steps: A2-2 is gated on
observed writer rollout; reverting A4-2 requires the reverse-direction corpus diff recorded first.
A6 is gated on an off-repo backup bundle plus a fail-closed epoch guard, and its resumability is
explicitly **none** — mitigated by running every correctness assertion on a scratch clone before
anything is published.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed `bindings.json` version is **<=25% of the pre-change
      baseline measured by the same method** (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo,
      repack `--window=250 --depth=50`, compute `(pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)`). Baseline today 12.79 KB.
      Verify: the measurement script recorded in the child ticket.
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: integration against a stateful fake asserting
      file bytes and commit count, not call counts.
- [ ] `baseline_advanced_at` is absent from every entry written by `set_baseline`, and no `src/`
      reference to it remains. Verify: `grep -r baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty) — the read-only path must not persist a migration.
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the same
      verdict as its normalized-string equivalent. This test does not exist today; the existing
      cells use flat strings only, so a no-op-on-strings normalizer would pass while proving
      nothing. Tier: integration through the real production comparison path.
- [ ] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over >=4 real snapshot pairs shows zero
      difference in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect, **and** the reverse-direction
      diff is recorded as the A4-2 rollback artifact.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` is **<=800 LOC** after the rotation extraction (it is at exactly 800
      today; the locked module-size gate fails the build on 801).
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB**, `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded
      pre-rewrite tip tree, and commit and merge-commit counts are unchanged (measured at window
      time, not hardcoded).
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** (the assertion that actually proves non-resurrection) and
      `size-pack` growth is <1 MB.
- [ ] A clone on a stale epoch attempting to push **aborts and performs no merge** at **both**
      guarded sites (`sync._union_merge` and `push.py`'s non-FF retry). Tier: integration in two
      real temporary clones with divergent epochs.
- [ ] An ADR exists enumerating all three committed-format changes, the mixed-version protocol, the
      A2-2 gate, and each rollback boundary.
- [ ] The off-repo backup bundle exists and `git bundle verify` passes. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] Operator has confirmed zero active sessions and all `rebar-mcp` servers stopped before the
      reclaim window. **[operator-attested]**

file_impact.reason: epoch guard before its own merges

compiled_state.title: Bound tickets-store growth: make the committed .bridge_state cache cheap + one-time reclaim of the spent ~1 GiB
